markscheme.html:
a

Small bar magnet drawn at X, aligned tangentially to the field line. [1] The north pole of the small magnet points to the left (in the direction of the field line). [1]

Direction of field is from N to S.

b.i

The product of the magnetic field strength component perpendicular to a surface and the area of the surface. OR Φ = BAcosθ with all symbols defined.

b.ii

As the magnet approaches, the magnetic flux (linkage) through the loop changes. [1] By Faraday's law, a changing flux induces an emf (which is measured by the voltmeter). [1]

c.i

Recognizes that magnitude of emf is the gradient of the flux-time graph. [1] Draws a tangent at the steepest point of the graph (approx. t=0.25-0.3s). [1] Correct calculation of gradient, e.g., gradient ≈ (0.10 - 0.02) / (0.34 - 0.24) = 0.8 V. Accept answers in range 0.7 V to 0.9 V. [1]

Units must be correct. A large triangle should be used for the tangent.

c.ii

Entering: anti-clockwise (when viewed from above). [1] Leaving: clockwise (when viewed from above). [1]

Reasoning (not required but for clarity): On entry, downward flux increases, so induced field is upward (anti-clockwise current). On leaving, downward flux decreases, so induced field is downward (clockwise current).

d.i

The magnet enters the coil when its bottom end is 10 cm below its equilibrium position. The center of the magnet is then at y = -0.10 m. [1] Speed v = ω√(A² - y²) = 4π√(0.15² - (-0.10)²) ≈ 1.41 m s⁻¹. [1]

Based on image data A=0.15m, ω=4π rad/s. The draft answer is incorrect as it uses different parameters and assumes entry at y=0.

d.ii

Use of ω² = k/m. [1] m = k/ω² = 5.0 / (4π)² ≈ 0.0317 kg (or 32 g). [1]

Based on image data ω=4π rad/s and k=5.0 N/m. The draft answer is incorrect.

d.iii

The oscillation induces a current in the coil/resistor circuit, which dissipates the mechanical energy of the oscillator as thermal energy.

The question in the image is for 1 mark, not 2 as in the draft.

e.i

Energy in 1 year E = Pt = (1×10⁹ J/s) × (365×24×3600 s) ≈ 3.15×10¹⁶ J. [1] Number of fissions N = / = (3.15×10¹⁶ J) / (200×10⁶×1.602×10⁻¹⁹ J) ≈ 9.84×10²⁶. [1] Mass = N × (235 u) = (9.84×10²⁶) × (235 × 1.661×10⁻²⁷ kg) ≈ 385 kg. [1]

Allow use of 365.25 days. Allow calculation via moles. Final answer to 2 or 3 s.f.

e.ii

The kinetic energy of the fission products is converted to thermal energy in the reactor core/coolant. [1] This thermal energy is used to create steam, which drives a turbine connected to an electrical generator. [1]

question.html:
9. Two bar magnets are aligned with their opposite poles facing each other. The diagram shows the pattern of the magnetic field lines produced by the magnets, without specifying their direction. A small magnet is placed at X. The original magnetic field pattern is negligibly disturbed.

a Draw a small magnet at X with correct orientation and polarity in the field between two bar magnets. [2]

b.i State the definition of magnetic flux. [1]

b.ii Explain the voltmeter reading as a magnet approaches a loop using Faraday's law. [2]

c.i Use the flux-time graph to determine maximum induced emf. [3]

c.ii State current direction in the loop as magnet enters and leaves. [2]

d.i Calculate the speed of the magnet when it is about to enter the coil. [2]

d.ii Determine the mass of the magnet. [2]

d.iii

A resistor is connected between the ends of the coil and the oscillations die away.

Explain why the oscillations of the magnet die away.

[1]

e.i Calculate minimum mass of U-235 needed for a 1 GW power plant for one year if each fission releases 200 MeV. [3]

e.ii Explain how the energy from fission is harnessed in a nuclear power plant. [2]
